LargeChance.Note: the chance an offered deed is large (Skill here is the base skill, without racial bonus)

Rules.Note: Per craft a player holds up to MaxCached waiting offers (they start full); one more is earned every DelayHours. Asking a vendor (its 'bulk order info' entry) gives an offer at once if DelayHours have passed since the last, else spends a cached one, else says how long to wait. Selling items to the vendor offers one with OfferChance. A declined offer is given back (SeriousFun: RefundBulkOrder). Handing in a filled deed pays its Gold into the bank and its Fame, and its Points either go to one reward now (spend them on a Rewards entry costing no more) or are banked at BankedShare of their value (small x0.02, large x0.2) to buy rewards from the bank later; a pending turn-in must be claimed before the next one. A vendor only deals in its own craft's deeds.
Rules.VariablesNote: Formula variables: Skill (craft skill 0-120), Quantity (10/15/20), Exceptional (0/1), Material (index into the craft's Materials, 0 = none), ItemCount (1 small, else the large set's item count), TypePoints (RewardTypes points of the deed's first item type, 0 if none). Gold formulas also use Gold (the table value) and BuyPrice (the item's shop price).

Small.Note: A list is picked by its Chance (Skill = the player's craft skill, the higher of base skill and racial bonus); then the amount from Amounts (the first row whose MinSkill the player has; one of Values at random). On a list that UsesMaterial (MaterialRoll: the chance it's rolled at all) and from 70.1 skill, a material is drawn by MaterialChances up to 20 times until one is drawn whose MaterialSkill the player has (None needs nothing); otherwise none. Exceptional is asked with ExceptionalChance on lists marked Exceptional. The item is one at random of the list's items the player can craft (has every required skill and a success chance above 0), and, if exceptional is asked, can make exceptional (exceptional chance above 0).

Large.Note: One of the Sets at random (equal odds; no skill check on the items), the amount from Amounts; a set that UsesMaterial draws one material by MaterialChances (no skill gate); a set marked Exceptional asks for exceptional with ExceptionalChance. The player needs every item of the set at that amount (and quality, material) to fill it.

Fame.Expr: trunc(((Quantity == 10 ? 10 : Quantity == 15 ? 25 : Quantity == 20 ? 50 : 0) + Exceptional * 200 + (ItemCount > 1 ? TypePoints : 0) + (Material >= 1 && Material <= 8 ? 200 + 50 * (Material - 1) : 0)) / 50) * trunc(((Quantity == 10 ? 10 : Quantity == 15 ? 25 : Quantity == 20 ? 50 : 0) + Exceptional * 200 + (ItemCount > 1 ? TypePoints : 0) + (Material >= 1 && Material <= 8 ? 200 + 50 * (Material - 1) : 0)) / 50)

Gold.Note: Gold paid into the bank for a filled deed. A small deed whose item a vendor sells (its BuyPrice, the shop price) pays SmallBuyPrice exactly. Otherwise Gold = Tables[t].Values[Row][Column], with t = SmallTable for a small deed or the set's GoldTable for a large one, plus 1 when the deed is exceptional; the payout is Spread (rand inclusive, like Utility.RandomMinMax: 90% to 111% of Gold). The table labels are ServUO's comments and don't always match how the code indexes them (the code is what's exported).
